nodes.label: DDD-First Workspace Operating Policy
nodes.rationale: To prevent future code drift and costly refactoring, every phase of code writing is subject to mandatory DDD-first rules — learned from 2026-05-19 enforcement experience. DDD documentation is treated as mandatory source code and the single source of truth.

nodes.label: Mandatory Pre-Work Gate
nodes.rationale: Before editing any file, agents must read canonical DDD references in fixed order to prevent drift between code and domain language. If references are missing, stop non-DDD edits and bootstrap first.

nodes.label: Dependency Lockfile Determinism Gate
nodes.rationale: Never hand-edit lockfiles. Regenerate only through npm commands to keep npm ci deterministic in CI/CD. Both root and frontend lockfiles must stay in sync.

nodes.label: Sync Dev After Release CI Workflow
PDA Framework (Persona, Desire, Awareness)
nodes.rationale: Framework for awareness-based angle generation applied in every step: Persona analysis, Desire mapping, and Awareness stage classification. Combined with evidence synthesis across social, review, search, and sales signals, plus four decision parameters (ROI, differentiation, ease of communication, credibility).

nodes.label: Five Awareness Levels
nodes.rationale: Deterministic five-level progression from low to high purchase readiness: Completely Unaware to Problem Aware to Solution Aware to Product Aware to Most Aware. Each level has strict nature check, primary ad job, and messaging posture. Boundary rules prevent misclassification based on generic ad exposure or review consumption alone.

CSRF Fail-Closed Startup Invariant
nodes.rationale: A security control that can be silently bypassed by misconfiguration violates the fail-closed principle. Security invariants must be enforced at startup (constructor/factory boundary), not deferred to per-request execution.

nodes.label: Unified Frontend Data Access Layer
nodes.rationale: Reduce code duplication across frontend HTTP helpers, endpoint hardcoding, data loading patterns, and query param parsers without introducing external data fetching libraries.

nodes.label: Geometric Admin Debug & Monitoring
nodes.rationale: Define admin debugging and monitoring strategies to verify that Geometric outputs are real and correct, with focus on crawling verification per session, AI Overview extraction validation, and structured error tracking.

Meta Ads Output Format Evolution Proposal
nodes.rationale: Evolution from 4 variant lengths to cluster→angle→awareness system with user-controlled copy length (short/medium/long form) for better targeting precision, operational flexibility, and Meta Ads 2024+ algorithm alignment.

nodes.label: Error Logging And UX Feedback Improvements Proposal
nodes.rationale: Production log analysis revealed three error classes during generation/run execution that are functional but poorly observable: idempotency_conflict, ECONNRESET, and duplicate step dispatch. Structured logging and improved UX feedback are needed for debug correlation.

nodes.label: SERP API Integration for Geometric
nodes.rationale: Google systematically blocks Puppeteer requests (sourceCount: 0, paaCount: 0). Commercial SERP APIs handle anti-bot complexity. Architectural split: Geometric uses SERP API only via ApiService; Puppeteer remains available for future non-Google tool contexts. No silent fallback.

nodes.label: ApiServiceAccessMode = 'query-param' (BLOCKER-001 resolved)
nodes.rationale: SerpAPI requires api_key as query parameter. Extended ApiServiceAccessMode with 'query-param', added tokenParamName field, and modified api-acquisition.adapter.ts to inject token as query param.

nodes.label: Kysely (Typed SQL Builder)
nodes.rationale: Reduces repeated string concatenation patterns for SQL WHERE/SET/pagination clauses and improves type safety in adapter-level projections with one query-construction style across repositories.

nodes.label: Zod (Backend Validation)
nodes.rationale: Frontend already uses Zod extensively; extending it to backend request parsing creates one validation language across FE and BE, replaces manual parse helpers with schema-based coercion and typed output.

nodes.label: Variant B — Private-Network Same-Origin via frontend/server.mjs
nodes.rationale: Browser sees single origin (frontend), proxy routes /auth, /generation, /api, /admin/users to backend via Railway private network. Eliminates CORS complexity, enables SameSite=Lax cookies, reduces cross-origin attack surface.

nodes.label: MUI v9 Theming Engine
nodes.rationale: Unified theming managed by MUI v9 via cssVariables: true + colorSchemes: { light, dark }. MUI writes CSS custom properties on [data-theme] selector. Removed custom ThemeProvider in favor of native MUI provider with defaultMode: 'system'.

nodes.label: ToolFormRegistry (Registry Pattern)
nodes.rationale: Declarative map of ToolFormConfig for each tool. Eliminates ~95% code duplication between tool pages; adding a new tool requires ~30 minutes with just a registry entry + wrapper page.

nodes.label: Non-Streaming Generation Migration
nodes.rationale: As of June 2026, tool generation migrated to non-streaming model (POST /generation/run, JSON response). Streaming path (SSE) remains dormant for future uses. Reason: non-streaming simplifies error handling and reduces connection management complexity.

nodes.label: GenerationSession FE Liveness Dependency Weakness
nodes.rationale: Generation flow completion remains partially dependent on Frontend/UI liveness signals. If the client disconnects or the Tool Workspace is interrupted, session completion can remain tied to FE-driven progression instead of a backend-owned continuation path. Introduce a backend-owned session batch continuation job that can resume and complete eligible GenerationSession runs without requiring FE presence.

nodes.label: Tool Workspace Stuck in Generation Mode After Interruptions
nodes.rationale: Interruption/error scenarios can leave the page in a non-recoverable running state with insufficient unblock feedback for the user. Add a deterministic fail-close recovery policy that forces transition out of running, surfaces actionable DispatchError, and exposes explicit user recovery actions (retry/reset/reload-session).

nodes.label: OrchestrateArtifactCache Redis Cache Strategy
nodes.rationale: Redis Hash cache for /api/tools/orchestrate provides O(1) lookup with cross-instance consistency, eliminating DB queries during active sessions. Cache-first lookup with graceful fallback to DB path on cache miss or Redis failure. Fire-and-forget cache population avoids adding latency to the critical path. TTL: 14400s.

nodes.label: Documentation Governance DDD and Ubiquitous Language
DDD-First Naming Gate
nodes.rationale: Use canonical terms only. Do not introduce synonyms as primary terms. Keep deprecated aliases only when explicitly documented in the decision log. Ensures naming coherence across code, contracts, and documentation.

nodes.label: Active vs Archive Gate
nodes.rationale: Active documents are only those required for current architecture, runtime, testing, and governance operation. Superseded snapshots, historical investigations, completed plans, and duplicate variants must be archived.

nodes.label: Context Ownership Gate
nodes.rationale: Each document must have one primary bounded-context ownership. Cross-context concepts must reference the context map and translation boundaries. Avoid multi-context scope creep in a single document.

nodes.label: Link Simplicity Gate
nodes.rationale: Avoid link maze patterns. Keep one index entrypoint and a short core-first reading path. Prefer stable directory links for large archives over long per-file enumerations.

nodes.label: Documentation DDD-First Governance Model
nodes.rationale: Deterministic governance model using Domain-Driven Design and Ubiquitous Language for project documentation. Four gates: DDD-First Naming (canonical terms only), Context Ownership (one bounded context per doc), Active vs Archive (operational docs only), Link Simplicity (short core-first path). Mandatory canonical references: glossary, bounded context map, decision log.

nodes.label: Frontend UX Determinism and Unification Code Review
XState Explicit Error States Pattern
nodes.rationale: Error strings instead of explicit error states in XState machines create non-deterministic UX. The pattern is to use compound child states (e.g. idle.clean / idle.failed) so UX behavior is deterministic from state.matches() — no context.error !== null checks needed. Applied to tool-page.machine.ts, briefing-upload.machine.ts, and auth-session.machine.ts per ADR-003.

nodes.label: DataTableView Pattern
nodes.rationale: Canonical UI pattern for list-oriented domain entities: query hook retrieves ordered entity list, toolbar exposes filters/actions, presentational table renders rows with atomic action components, mutation hooks handle CRUD outcomes. All instances must use shared primitives (Surface, TopBar, ListingTableSection). Prevents divergent table/list implementations across admin pages.

nodes.label: FeedbackChannel Three-Channel Model
nodes.rationale: Three deterministic feedback channels: inline-action (per-action feedback near controls), page-state (LoadingStateMessage/ErrorStateMessage/EmptyStateMessage in page body), global (cross-page mutation confirmations). Preserves context fidelity: action-scoped failures remain near actions, query/list states remain in-page.

SerpApi-Only Crawling Pattern
nodes.rationale: The Geometric tool uses SerpApi exclusively for SERP data extraction with no Puppeteer fallback. If SerpApi fails, the crawling process stops with an error. This improves reliability by reducing dependency on Puppeteer's anti-bot detection circumvention and eliminates browser automation overhead.
